title: DataPilot AI
problem: Answering questions about operational data can mean jumping between SQL clients, Python scripts, and separate ETL tools.
role: Independent project — designed and built the conversational data assistant and its multi-agent workflows.
process: Built a LangGraph router that sends database questions to a schema-aware SQL analyst and extraction or transformation requests to an ETL analyst. Gemini powers routing and generation; SQL is checked for read-only intent before execution.
outcome: A local prototype that brings natural-language PostgreSQL analysis, API extraction, and Pandas-powered file transformations into one conversational workflow. SQL checks are a prototype safeguard, not a production-grade policy engine.

title: CryptoGeek
problem: Crypto prices move quickly, and comparing market history across a growing list of coins can feel overwhelming.
role: Full-stack development, from the market-tracking experience to account and watchlist flows.
process: Brought price history, coin discovery, and a personal wishlist into one focused experience, with sign-up and sign-in for returning users.
outcome: A single place to explore historical trends across 100+ cryptocurrencies and keep a personal shortlist close at hand.

title: NameIt
problem: Naming a new project is hard enough without repeatedly leaving the brainstorming process to check domain availability.
process: Created a lightweight React app that helps people explore project-name ideas and moves naturally from inspiration to a domain search.
outcome: A shorter path from a name idea to checking available domains through Namecheap.

title: Digital Whiteboard
problem: Sometimes the quickest way to explain an idea is to draw it, without opening a heavyweight design tool.
process: Built a browser-based drawing surface with the Canvas API and JavaScript, keeping the focus on an immediate, hands-on workspace.
outcome: A lightweight place to sketch and communicate ideas directly in the browser.

title: Memespark
problem: Making a quick meme should be playful and approachable, not a detour through complicated editing software.
process: Made a focused meme-creation experience around a browsable collection of more than 100 templates.
outcome: A low-friction starting point for creating and sharing a meme from a familiar template.
